title: Direct Observation of Light-Driven Structural Transformations in Catalytic Nanomaterials via In Situ Gas-Cell TEM
content: Understanding the atomic-scale dynamics of metal catalysts under reactive conditions is critical for advancing catalytic applications [1]. In situ gas-cell transmission electron microscopy (GC-TEM) has emerged as a powerful platform for directly imaging the atomic-scale structural dynamics while simultaneously monitoring reaction products during heterogeneous catalytic processes under real-world catalytic conditions by integrating controlled gas environments, heating, and light illumination [2]. Here, we employ a novel in situ GC-TEM platform equipped with an optical-fiber-coupled atmospheric TEM holder and an ultra-thin silicon nitride microchip [3] to explore the real-time structural evolution of catalytic nanomaterials (e.g., aluminum nanocrystals (Al NCs) decorated with platinum (Pt), as shown in Fig. 1) under controlled reaction conditions. The combination of in situ imaging and spectroscopy provides a unique opportunity to study light-driven and gas-induced structural transformations in catalytic nanomaterials (e.g., surface restructuring by desorption induced by electronic transition (DIET) processes or dynamics of active sites), offering insights into fundamental reaction mechanisms and guiding future catalyst design strategies.
